title: the same selecting operators over two local objects, over a trusted foreign tag, and around a trusted callee named directly, introduce no boundary refusal and the program runs
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary': the checked panic case is added by 'calling an unannotated foreign runtime value', and 'Trusted @throws {never} metadata opts out.' Nothing here is such a value, so nothing here may be refused. This is the over-correction guard for `a-selected-foreign-constructor-property-and-tag-are-still-foreign`: that case requires the operand walk behind `??`, `||`, `&&`, a conditional and a comma to start finding foreign values it previously missed, and the cheapest way to satisfy it is to refuse the OPERATOR — every selection, foreign or not. This file is what that costs, and it is not hypothetical: this repository has shipped seven over-corrections. THE OUTPUT IS THE EVIDENCE. `andOverLocals` prints `9` where every other local line prints `3`, because `&&` yields its RIGHT operand — so the case observes which branch actually ran rather than merely that something was returned. `localTag` returns the constant `L`, which appears nowhere in the expected output, so the three `a` lines say the TRUSTED tag was selected and executed by every one of `??`, `||` and the conditional; a lowering that picked the wrong branch prints `L` and the case goes red. `4` and `6` come from two calls to `double`, one named directly and one through a parenthesis, which is the pair that says a trusted foreign callee stays usable at the two spellings that are not selections. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN, and the omission is a measured one rather than an oversight: a trusted foreign callee reached through a SELECTOR. `(double ?? localDouble)(2)` is refused on both backends with `SMITHERS1507` — the trust marker is about the call, not about the evaluation order of the expression that selects the callee — so it is not a negative and it does not belong here. It has its own case, `a-selected-trusted-foreign-callee-is-still-not-order-safe`. It also omits the comma spelling over two locals, for a harness reason worth writing down: `(second, first).retries` is rejected by stock TypeScript as `TS2695` ('left side of comma operator is unused and has no side effects'), and an `output` case must survive a stock check of the EMITTED module set, so the comma selector is exercised only in the refusal sibling, where the frontend refuses first and the emit check is never reached. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the third declared stdout line from `9` to `3` — making all four local lines identical, which is exactly what a lowering that yielded the left operand of `&&` would print — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 0539dddfe588cbe060b45d091c765cc434a2d5d2c2ce1668a6101a35534ce999 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently).
